identity.real_world_identity_notes: McLaren MP4/12 of 1997, running Mercedes-Benz FO110E and FO110F V10s with a McLaren six-speed longitudinal semi-automatic sequential gearbox.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies neither, and a clutch is still needed to pull away, which is the semi-automatic pattern of the era.

The unsuffixed identity is held in SimHub's stored inventory from an earlier observation and is carried here. An earlier note said no other configuration had been reported, which was drawn from the live diagnostics log alone and missed the stored one.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mclaren-mercedes-mp4-12-high-downforce.20260815t234827608z-e8100197 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by a registered source.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the MP4/12 and its transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source gives a McLaren six-speed longitudinal semi-automatic sequential, and the live drive selected six paddle gears with automatic cut and blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Early paddle semi-automatic: the gearbox works its own clutch and yours is only for the start. It cuts the upshift and blips the downshift, so once you are away the pedals are throttle and brake.
